title: Rehosting exit & transition ops notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to capture negotiation anchors and fallback language for customers who may rehost or require data extraction / redeploy assistance. Focused on transitions for Dedicated/Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).

High-level concerns to surface early (order matters):
- Data portability & format: insist on clear export format (NDJSON + metadata manifest). Delivery window: specify staging export within 30 days of request.
- Validation period: buyer gets 45-day validation window after export where Redwood must support reproducibility issues; we provide two support engineer days at no charge.
- Cost of export & egress: prefer to absorb export in most enterprise deals, but fallback: cap customer-only egress fees to a single one-time fee (e.g., $X) or at-cost with 10% margin. Avoid open-ended pass-throughs.
- KMS / keying: no forced escrow unless regulated. If customer wants key escrow for model artifacts, propose HSM-backed escrow with mutual TLS and explicit custody transfer steps.
- Migration assistance & runbook: require customer to submit desired target architecture and provide 30 days of transition assistance (2x SE days included) — additional days billable at standard SOW rates.
- Subprocessor list / supplier chain: provide current subprocessor list at time of export; allow for 30-day notice if new subprocessors are introduced during transition.
- Hardware decommission certificate: customer may request certificate of secure wipe for any dedicated appliances we control; provide within 15 days post-decomm for a fixed fee.

Negotiation anchors / suggested clause language (working drafts):
1) Data Export / Portability
- "Upon Customer's written request, Redwood will produce a complete export of Customer Data in machine-readable NDJSON format with associated manifest and crc32 checksums within 30 days. Redwood will retain an export copy for 14 days to assist migration; thereafter Redwood may securely delete it unless otherwise agreed."

2) Validation & Reproducibility Period
- "Customer shall have 45 calendar days after receipt of the export to validate the data. Redwood will reasonably cooperate and provide up to 16 hours of technical assistance at no additional charge to help reproduce key artifacts. Issues discovered after the validation period may be addressed under a paid support engagement except where caused by Redwood's gross negligence."

3) Assistance & Onboarding for Rehost
- "Redwood will provide transition assistance as described in the Service Attachment: 30 days of transition support (including two dedicated SE days) to assist with environment setup and verification. Additional assistance shall be provided under a Statement of Work at then-current rates."

4) KMS and Key Handover (if requested)
- "If Customer requires key handover, parties will agree a mutually acceptable HSM-backed transfer protocol. Redwood will not retain plaintext keys after successful handover and will confirm with a signed Key Handover Certificate."

5) Service Credits tied to Data Recovery Failure (limited)
- "If Redwood fails to deliver a conformant export within 30 days and Customer demonstrates unrecoverable data loss attributable to Redwood, Redwood will provide a one-time service credit equal to one month of average monthly charges for the last 3 months, as the sole and exclusive remedy for that failure."

Redlines / positions (BATNA / walkaways):
- BATNA (preferred): Accept the export/validation language above, Redwood absorbs export cost for enterprise deals, limited assistance included.
- Compromise: Redwood charges a capped export fee and provides 16 free support hours.
- Walkaway: Contract that requires indefinite archival of customer exports on Redwood infrastructure without compensation, or unlimited post-exit support liability — escalate.

Practical negotiation tactics / talking points:
- Reframe export timing as "operational safety" not a concession — we need clear windows to schedule extraction jobs.
- Offer a short free-validation period (45d) to reduce buyer anxiety; tie additional assistance to SOWs.
- Ask the customer for concrete target environment details early (cloud provider, region, orchestration), this limits scope creep.
- Use SOW line items for any on-prem appliance decommissioning work (certificate generation, physical wipe logistics). Keep fees predictable.
- If customer pushes for KMS escrow, require mutual audit and a third-party HSM provider; avoid ad-hoc key copies.

Open questions / items to confirm internally before committing:
- Default export format for embeddings/weights vs. structured logs. Need input from Applied ML on size and optimal chunking (ticket MIGRATE-412).
- Standard pricing for export/egress cap — propose $2k one-time for medium customers, higher for >50TB. Confirm with Finance.
- Template Key Handover Certificate — coordinate with Security.
- Standard language for subprocessor notice window (30 days?) — coordinate with Privacy.

References / quick links (for my follow-up):
- MIGRATE-412 (Jira) — estimated runtime for 10TB export job.
- Confluence: Rehosting Playbook (internal) — runbooks and checklist.
- Slack: #cust-migrations thread (link pinned).

Notes to self (negotiation day):
- Start call with timeline commitments, not legalese. "We can get your full export ready within 30 days and give you 45 days to validate" lands well.
- If asked to reduce validation window, offer to add two paid support days instead.
- Document any custom export schema in SOW/Annex to avoid disputes later.

Quick sample negotiation script snippets:
- "We want to make your transition low-friction — our standard is 30 days for delivery and 45 days for validation with two SE days included. If you need extended hands-on help we can add an SOW so you only pay for what you use."
- "For KMS handovers we do a HSM-backed transfer and issue a handover certificate; we won’t retain plaintext keys afterwards."

End of notes. Keep this as my working copy; will draft a cleaned clause pack once Finance/Security chime in.
